messages:
From: Anna Weber <anna.weber@stellarsystems.com>

Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00Z
Subject: EU geofence & deletion timeline for hosted API

Hi Michael,

We're evaluating Redwood for PII-handling use cases in the EU. A few specific questions from our security and privacy teams — can you confirm details for the hosted API?

1) If Stellar requests deletion of all data tied to a tenant (API keys + tenant_id), what is the complete timeline for: primary logs, backups/snapshots, and system/audit logs?
2) Are backups and snapshots stored in the EU region only when we use the hosted API?
3) How are encryption keys handled for hosted customers (Redwood-managed vs customer-managed)? If BYOK is available, what changes for deletion?
4) Does the model KV cache or any transient in-memory state persist beyond a single request?
5) What evidence/certificate do you provide when deletion is complete? We need something we can attach to our records and present to auditors.

Thanks — can you put timelines in business days and list any caveats?

Best,
Anna Weber
Security Program Manager
Stellar Systems

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: EU geofence & deletion timeline for hosted API

Anna — thanks for the detailed questions. I’ll summarize high-level answers here and then loop in Ops/Security for any nitty-gritty.

TL;DR (short): Primary tenant data is removed within 3 business days after a verified deletion request; backups are scheduled for removal and typically purged within 30 business days; snapshots/long-term cold backups are included in the removal process and can take up to 90 calendar days in edge cases. Hosted API by default stores copies in the region you select (EU) and uses Redwood-managed encryption keys. We can provide a deletion certificate after the work is complete.

Full answers:
- Primary data (request logs, conversation payloads, stored prompt history linked to tenant_id) — removed from the active serving datastore within 72 hours (3 business days) after we validate the deletion request and complete identity verification.
- Backups & incremental restore points — once a deletion job is opened, the dataset is flagged and included in the next backup retention trimming window. For hosted customers this process means removal within ~30 business days in most cases; some long-term snapshot/archival layers can extend to ~90 calendar days depending on the archival tier and current restore windows.
- Snapshots & cold archives — if your account was included in a periodic snapshot, it will be scheduled for deletion but may remain in immutable storage until the snapshot's retention expiry; we provide the snapshot IDs we purge so you can reconcile.
- Region/geofence — hosted API stores primary and backup data in the region you select (we have EU regions available). We do NOT copy primary customer data out of the region for routine operations. For cross-region replication (only performed for specific DR configurations) we will document prior to setup.
- Encryption/KMS — hosted customers default to Redwood-managed keys (AES keys managed by our cloud provider). For Dedicated/Private we support customer-managed keys (BYOK) and HSM integrations. If you require BYOK for hosted, that’s available as an enterprise add-on; deletion semantics differ slightly because key destruction is in the customer's control — see note below.
- KV cache / model cache — runtime KV caches are ephemeral in-memory structures tied to active sessions; they are not persisted to long-term storage. Any prefix caching we perform is stored in an encrypted cache that follows the same deletion flow as primary payloads.
- Audit & access logs — system-level access/audit logs are retained for 180 days by default (this may be shorter with specific contracts). These logs record API key usage and administrative accesses and are retained for compliance; we can provide redacted copies when needed.
- Evidence & certificate — once deletion completes we will generate a deletion certificate (signed, timestamped) that lists the tenant_id, deletion request id, snapshot IDs removed, and the timeline. We can provide this as a PDF and also record the deletion job in your HubSpot record.

Next steps I recommend:
1) If you want BYOK for hosted, Neha (cc'd) can scope the enterprise add-on.
2) I’ll open a support deletion job if you want to run a test tenant erasure; we can generate a certificate and share the Drive folder with logs/snapshot IDs.

I’m looping Naomi from Security to confirm the backup/snapshot windows and the exact wording we use in the deletion certificate.

—Michael

On Apr 18, 2027, Michael Grant wrote:
> - Backups & incremental restore points — once a deletion job is opened, the dataset is flagged and included in the next backup retention trimming window. For hosted customers this process means removal within ~30 business days in most cases; some long-term snapshot/archival layers can extend to ~90 calendar days depending on the archival tier and current restore windows.

Small clarification from Security/Operations: the typical operating window we reliably commit to for incremental backups is 30 calendar days (not business days). The 30-day window covers standard incremental backups and warm standby copies. Long-term archival snapshots (cold storage) are handled on their snapshot lifecycle and should be considered up to 90 calendar days in edge cases.

Also — hosted BYOK is available only under an enterprise contract with an onboarding period; for deletion evidence in those cases the customer is expected to coordinate key destruction (we can assist the workflow but cannot unilaterally destroy a customer key).

Hi Anna — following up with the corrected timeline and next steps. Attached is a template deletion certificate we’ll sign after we run a deletion job (attached as PDF).

Consolidated timeline (final):
- Primary data purge: completed within 3 business days after verification of deletion request.
- Incremental backups & warm copies: scheduled removal within 30 calendar days after the purge job is opened.
- Long-term snapshots/cold archives: may take up to 90 calendar days in isolated cases; we will provide snapshot IDs and removal dates.
- Audit/access logs: retained 180 days by default (we can discuss shorter retention through contract) — note these are separate from customer data payloads and are retained for security/audit purposes.
- KV/model cache: ephemeral; not written to persistent storage beyond the primary data flow.

Operational notes / caveats:
- BYOK: hosted BYOK requires an enterprise add-on and onboarding. When BYOK is used, key destruction is controlled by the customer and will alter the timeline for cryptographic erasure. We will coordinate a joint runbook.
- Cross-region replication: if you enable cross-region DR then copies will exist in the DR region and must be included in deletion; we document and schedule that as part of the deletion job.
- Third-party backups (if configured): some optional partner backup providers may have independent retention; we’ll enumerate these in the deletion certificate where applicable.

Evidence & delivery:
- After the deletion job completes we’ll provide: signed deletion_certificate_stellar_20270420.pdf (attached), a list of snapshot IDs removed, the HubSpot ticket ID (HUBSPOT-12345678), and a Drive folder with logs for reconciliation. We aim to deliver the certificate within 5 business days of job completion.

If this matches your needs I’ll open the deletion job and initiate a test erasure against a non-production tenant so you can validate the certificate workflow. Please confirm and I’ll schedule the run.
